title: Variables, Initialization and Assignment
learningObjectives: Explain the key idea in variables, initialization and assignment.
Identify suitable syntax and type/value rules.
Trace each example and predict the result.
Use the concept in a small practical program.
Avoid a common mistake related to initialization, constness or type choice.

understand.concept: A variable is a named object that stores a value. In C++, declare a variable with a type and a name, and initialize it before use. Assignment changes an object's stored value after it has been created. Initialization and assignment are different operations.
understand.whyItMatters: These fundamentals appear in nearly every C++ program and help make code predictable, readable and correct.
understand.analogy: Think of a labeled container: its label identifies what it is meant to hold, and its rules determine what can be put inside or changed.
understand.analogyLimit: Real C++ types have language-defined rules, conversions, representation and lifetime that a physical container analogy cannot capture.
understand.explain:
## Variables
A declaration introduces a name and its type. Initialization gives an object its starting value. Use braces for clear initialization where practical, for example `int count{3};`.

## Assignment
After a variable exists, `count = 5;` assigns a new value. Compound assignment such as `count += 2;` updates it using an operation.

## Naming and safety
Choose names that explain what the value represents. Avoid using uninitialized local variables; their values are not automatically useful defaults. Prefer initialization at declaration.

hints: Use names that explain the value.
Use const when a value should not be reassigned.

questions.prompt: Why initialize a variable when declaring it?
options: To give it a known starting value
To make the variable name longer
questions.answer: To give it a known starting value
questions.explanation: Initialization establishes the initial value and prevents use of an indeterminate local value.

The value is always stored as text
questions.answer: The object cannot be modified through that name after initialization
questions.explanation: const prevents modification through that name.

questions.prompt: Which type is commonly used for true/false values?
Which type is commonly used for fractional measurements?
What is a good type-selection practice?
options: Choose a type based on value meaning and range
Assume all types have identical size
questions.answer: Choose a type based on value meaning and range
questions.explanation: Types differ in representation, range and operations.
